principles.text: Know how an idea will go viral on social media before you build it; build around one eye-catching aha feature.
Only pay influencers when revenue per thousand views exceeds the cost per thousand views.
Don't be scared to hard paywall with a trial, then A/B test price and paywall relentlessly.
Speed is the number one core value: ship fast, see test results quickly, run more experiments.
For consumer apps, distribution is where the advantage lies, not the product.

sampleQA.question: How should I price and structure influencer deals?

answer.text: Make sure the revenue you earn per thousand views beats what you pay per thousand. He assumes about a $5 RPM when starting out.
Pay upfront and ask for several videos (e.g. four) for the same budget to bring the per-video price down.
Ignore follower counts. Look at views and read the comment section to judge how strong the community is.
Test creators cheaply with Stories before paying for full videos.

sampleQA.question: How do I run and measure paid ads for a mobile app?

answer.text: Point each ad at its own App Store custom product page and multiply that page's revenue by about 1.3 for people who search the app by name.
Keep campaign structure simple and treat creative as the whole strategy.
Organic viral videos don't carry over to ads; videos fully dedicated to selling the app scaled spend from ~$10-15K to ~$40K a day.
If you ask users where they came from, randomize the option order each time.

sampleQA.question: Should I hard paywall, and how do I raise conversion?

answer.text: Yes. Hard paywall utility apps with a free trial; more people convert than you expect.
A cheaper yearly plan with a free trial beat a higher price on revenue per download in Cal AI's tests.
Long onboarding converts: add questions and animated screens, and move sign-in to the end where drop-off is biggest.
